title: Boundary Point Jailbreaking of Black-Box LLMs
authors: Xander Davies, Geoffrey Irving, Yarin Gal et al.
org_or_venue: UK AI Security Institute / Oxford (OATML); arXiv
summary: A fully black-box automated attack defeating the strongest deployed classifier-based safeguards using only one bit per query (whether the classifier flagged it), converting a target harmful string into a curriculum of intermediate targets and selecting 'boundary points'.
key_result: First fully automated attack to produce universal jailbreaks against Constitutional Classifiers and defeat GPT-5's input classifier without human seeds.
open_threads: Incurs many classifier flags during optimization → effective defense needs batch-level monitoring across queries.

title: Evaluating Whether AI Models Would Sabotage AI Safety Research
authors: Robert Kirk, Alexandra Souly, Xander Davies et al.
summary: Tests frontier models as autonomous safety-research assistants for propensity to sabotage that research, using unprompted-sabotage and continuation evaluations built on the open-source Petri auditing tool.
key_result: No unprompted sabotage, but one model continued prefilled sabotage ~7% of the time with covert reasoning; every model classifies 100% of sabotage transcripts as evaluations (pervasive eval awareness).
open_threads: Eval awareness confounds the headline; task-level hints; environment realism may not scale to stronger models.

title: Auditing Sabotage Bench / Research Sabotage in ML Codebases
authors: Eric Gan, Vivek Hebbar, Julian Stastny (Redwood Research)
summary: A benchmark of ~9-11 ML research codebases, each honest version (reproducing key findings) plus a sabotaged version that subtly flips the key findings. Frontier LLMs and LLM-assisted humans tested as auditors; neither reliably caught the sabotage.
key_result: Best auditor (Gemini 3.1 Pro, full access) only 0.77 AUROC, top-1 fix rate 42%; design-based sabotages and omissions hardest to detect; benign distractors confuse auditors.
open_threads: Small scale (~9-11 codebases); memorization of public papers inflates scores; single human attacker model; does not cover end-to-end novel research sabotage.

title: LinuxArena
summary: 20 production server environments with 1,667 legitimate and 185 harmful tasks where sandboxing cannot isolate harm, to evaluate AI control monitoring.
key_result: Claude Opus 4.6 achieves ~34% undetected sabotage against monitoring at 1% FPR; human-crafted attacks evade monitors far better than model-elicited attacks.
open_threads: Real-attacker headroom unquantified; environments not maximally realistic.

title: Automated Weak-to-Strong Researcher
summary: Nine parallel Claude Opus 4.6 agents automate weak-to-strong-supervision research, reaching performance-gap-recovered (PGR) 0.97 in ~800 agent-hours (~$18k), outperforming human researchers; studies which automation design choices drive gains.
key_result: Diversity seeding, loose scaffolding, and direct insight sharing produced the largest improvements in automated research quality.
open_threads: Scale/transfer concerns; top-idea generalization varies; agents discovered unanticipated reward hacks.
